draft.title: The women's movement in Australia
card: Women's rights campaigns in Australia changed women's role in work and public life. Women won the federal vote in 1902.
Before this, most women could not vote or stand in federal elections. The vote gave them a say in who made the nation's laws.
Equal pay rulings in 1969 and 1972 moved towards paying women the same as men for work of equal value. Before this, women were often paid less for the same work.
The Sex Discrimination Act in 1984 made it unlawful to treat people unfairly because of their sex in areas such as work.
draft.remember: Vote in 1902, equal pay rulings in 1969 and 1972, and the Sex Discrimination Act in 1984.

a.q: Which change in 1984 made it unlawful to treat people unfairly because of their sex?
a.why: The Sex Discrimination Act of 1984 made unfair treatment because of sex unlawful. The vote was won in 1902, and the pay rulings dealt with wages, not general discrimination.
a.clue: It is the only change in the 1980s.

b.q: Maria works in a factory in Geelong in 1960 and is paid less than a man doing the same job. Which later change moved towards ending this?
opts: The equal pay rulings of 1969 and 1972
The vote, which was won after 1969
b.why: The equal pay rulings of 1969 and 1972 moved towards paying women the same as men for work of equal value. The vote was about political rights and came earlier, in 1902.

b.best: The equal pay rulings of 1969 and 1972

problems.detail: "Women won the federal vote in 1902" is not true of all women. The Commonwealth Franchise Act 1902 excluded most Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander women (and men), who did not get the full federal vote until 1962. The card should say that the 1902 vote was for most, not all, women.

The stem gives the year 1984 and repeats the card's definition word for word, and the clue says it is the only 1980s change. A student can pick the answer by matching the date, without knowing the idea.

The Sex Discrimination Act 1984 made sex discrimination in employment unlawful, including in terms and conditions such as pay. A careful teacher could defend it as a later change that moved towards ending Maria's lower pay. The question should make clear it asks about the change aimed directly at wages, or replace this distractor.

proposal.title: The women's movement in Australia
card: In 1902 the Commonwealth Franchise Act gave most women the right to vote and stand in federal elections. Most Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander women and men were left out until 1962.
In 1969 the national wage tribunal ruled for equal pay for equal work. It helped women doing the same job as men, but not women in jobs done mostly by women.
In 1972 the tribunal ruled for equal pay for work of equal value. Jobs were compared by their skill and worth, so women in jobs few men did could also gain.

The Sex Discrimination Act 1984 made it unlawful to treat people unfairly because of their sex in areas such as hiring, promotion and education. Together these changes widened women's role in work and public life.
proposal.remember: The vote gave most women a political voice, the pay rulings dealt with wages, and the 1984 Act banned unfair treatment because of sex.

a.q: What did the 1972 equal pay ruling add to the 1969 ruling?
opts: Equal pay for work of equal value, not only the same job
Equal pay for women doing exactly the same job as men
A ban on refusing to hire people because of their sex
The right of most women to vote in federal elections
a.why: The 1969 ruling covered women doing the same job as men. The 1972 ruling went further, to work of equal value, so women in jobs done mostly by women could also gain. Equal pay for the same job was the 1969 step, not the new one.
a.clue: Think about women in jobs that few men did.

b.q: In 1990, a bank in Ballarat tells Jess it will not promote her to branch manager because it wants a man in the job. Which change made this unlawful?
b.why: Refusing a promotion because of sex is unfair treatment at work, which the 1984 Act made unlawful. The equal pay rulings dealt with wages for a job, not with who gets hired or promoted.
b.clue: Is the problem her pay, or how she is treated because of her sex?

a.best: Equal pay for work of equal value, not only the same job
